article_content: Recent news highlights the dangers posed by unlicensed tattoo parlours, operating without medical staff and often in places like pubs or garden sheds. These establishments, claimed by the Local Government Association, are a hub for health risks such as HIV and hepatitis, partly due to poor processes and equipment, plus a disregard for customer safety. With 29% of Britons aged 25 to 34 sporting a tattoo, the presence of over 1,500 licensed shops is vital. Yet, unlicensed operators are believed to be taking advantage of the growing trend, with authorities warning of fines and jail time of up to two years. In response, customers are advised to consult registered professionals and report any incidents involving unlicensed work to their local council.
